name: status
description: Display size, the user's default browser, permissions, pause state and your open windows.

description.macos: Running apps with their pid, bundle id and window count.
description.windows: Running apps with their pid, executable name and window count.

name: open_window
description: Open a NEW window of an app on your virtual display and return its window_id. Launches the app if needed. The user's existing windows are untouched. For browsers this is a new window in the user's own profile, signed in to the user's accounts. Open only apps and sites whose accounts the user has allowed for this task.

name: list_windows
description: Your windows. With `app`, also lists that app's other windows so you can pick one to borrow.

description.macos: Optional app name or bundle id.
description.windows: Optional app name or executable name.

name: borrow_window
description: Move one of the user's existing windows onto your display. Use only for single-window apps whose accounts the user has allowed for this task; release_window puts it back exactly where it was.

name: release_window
description: Finish with a window: closes windows you opened, returns borrowed ones to the user.

keep_open.description: Leave an opened window open on your display instead of closing it.

name: get_window_state
description: Accessibility tree of your window with numbered elements, plus a screenshot. An element keeps its number while it exists. After the first read of a window this lists only what changed since your last read (- removed, + added, ~ changed) unless you pass full=true; when most elements are new (another page) it lists everything and numbering restarts. Waits for the window to settle after an action.

full.description: List every element instead of the changes (default false).

name: screenshot
description: Screenshot of one of your windows, or of your whole display when window_id is omitted.

description.macos: Click an element (by number) or a point (x, y in window points). Element clicks use accessibility actions when the element supports them. A point click takes key focus in the app for a moment, so while the user is in that app it first waits for a pause in their input (see priority).
description.windows: Click an element (by number) or a point (x, y in window points). Element clicks use accessibility actions when the element supports them.

description.macos: Omit to wait for a pause in the user's input when they're in the same app (up to 3 s). "now" runs at once; only for steps that can't wait.
description.windows: Ignored on Windows, where steps never wait for the user.

name: set_value
description: Replace the value of a text field, slider or similar element through accessibility. Never touches keyboard focus.

description.macos: Perform a named accessibility action on an element, e.g. AXPress, AXShowMenu, AXConfirm, AXIncrement, AXDecrement, AXRaise, AXCancel.
description.windows: Perform a named UI Automation action on an element, e.g. Invoke, Toggle, Expand, Collapse, Select, ScrollIntoView, Focus.

action.description: Action name from the element's action list.

name: type_text
description: Type text into your window. With `element`, that element is focused first. Uses accessibility insertion when it works, otherwise keystrokes.

description.macos: Omit to wait for a pause in the user's input when they're in the same app (up to 3 s). "now" runs at once; only for steps that can't wait.
description.windows: Ignored on Windows, where steps never wait for the user.

description.macos: Press a key or shortcut in your window, e.g. key "return", or key "l" with modifiers ["cmd"]. While the user is in the same app it first waits for a pause in their input (see priority).
description.windows: Press a key or shortcut in your window, e.g. key "return", or key "l" with modifiers ["ctrl"].

key.description: Key name: a letter or digit, return, tab, space, escape, delete, forward_delete, up, down, left, right, home, end, page_up, page_down, f1-f12, or a punctuation character.

description.macos: Any of cmd, shift, option, ctrl, fn.
description.windows: Any of ctrl, shift, alt, win.

description.macos: Omit to wait for a pause in the user's input when they're in the same app (up to 3 s). "now" runs at once; only for steps that can't wait.
description.windows: Ignored on Windows, where steps never wait for the user.

name: scroll
description: Scroll in your window at an element or point. Positive dy scrolls down.

name: drag
description: Drag from one window point to another.

description.macos: Omit to wait for a pause in the user's input when they're in the same app (up to 3 s). "now" runs at once; only for steps that can't wait.
description.windows: Ignored on Windows, where steps never wait for the user.

name: press_menu_item
description: Choose a menu bar item of the window's app, applied to your window, e.g. path ["File", "Save…"].

path.description: Menu titles from the menu bar down.

description.macos: Omit to wait for a pause in the user's input when they're in the same app (up to 3 s). "now" runs at once; only for steps that can't wait.
description.windows: Ignored on Windows, where steps never wait for the user.

description.macos: Ask the user to take over a window (a sign-in, a password or 2FA code, a decision). A notification from the menu bar shows your reason, and the window comes onto the user's screen when they open it. Stop after calling this.
description.windows: Ask the user to take over a window (a sign-in, a password or 2FA code, a decision). Moves it onto the user's screen without activating it and shows your reason in the tray. Stop after calling this.

name: take_back
description: Move a handed-off window back onto your display once the user is done.

description.macos: Run several actions in order in one call, stopping at the first failure, then return the window's state (changes only, like get_window_state). Each action is an object with `tool` and that tool's arguments, e.g. {"tool": "click", "element": 6}, {"tool": "type_text", "text": "example.com\n"}, {"tool": "wait", "ms": 500}. Allowed tools: click, set_value, perform_action, type_text, press_key, scroll, drag, press_menu_item, wait. Element numbers refer to your last get_window_state. Steps that take key focus in an app the user is in wait for a pause in their input once, and back-to-back steps like that then run together.
description.windows: Run several actions in order in one call, stopping at the first failure, then return the window's state (changes only, like get_window_state). Each action is an object with `tool` and that tool's arguments, e.g. {"tool": "click", "element": 6}, {"tool": "type_text", "text": "example.com\n"}, {"tool": "wait", "ms": 500}. Allowed tools: click, set_value, perform_action, type_text, press_key, scroll, drag, press_menu_item, wait. Element numbers refer to your last get_window_state.

actions.description: Up to 40 actions: {"tool": name, ...that tool's arguments}.

full.description: List every element in that state instead of the changes (default false).

description.macos: "now" for every action that doesn't set its own priority: no waiting for the user. Only for steps that can't wait.
description.windows: Ignored on Windows, where steps never wait for the user.

screenshot.description: Include a screenshot with that state (default false).

state.description: Read the window's state after the actions (default true).

window_id.description: Window for every action that doesn't set its own window_id.

name: guard_report
description: Focus-guard events: anything that touched the user's focus, cursor or screen, with the action that caused it.
